error.signature: AI tells a tourist in Russia they can freely photograph military or official sites, or fly a drone, or share photos of a drone strike aftermath

verdict.summary: Photography at military, secure, or official sites (including airports) is illegal in Russia. Separately, publishing images or footage of drone strikes, their aftermath, or Russian military activity is severely restricted nationally and carries penalties up to imprisonment; several regions (Moscow, Murmansk) have layered their own decrees with specific fines on top. Drones require advance authorization from the aviation authority and 24-hour notice of the flight route, and some regions have banned civilian drone flights outright since 2022.

dead_ends.action: Photograph a military base, border post, checkpoint, or 'official site' (including an airport) for a tourist photo or social media
dead_ends.why_fails: Photography is illegal at any military, secure, or official site in Russia, including airports; this is enforced even when the site was only incidental to the shot the traveler intended to take.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers assume airports and everyday infrastructure are 'obviously fine' to photograph, as they would be at home.

dead_ends.action: Post or share photos or video of a drone strike, its aftermath, or Russian military operations while in Russia, including on personal social media
dead_ends.why_fails: Publishing or distributing information, including images, related to the Russian armed forces or military operations, including strike aftermath, is severely restricted nationally and can lead to fines or imprisonment of up to 15 years. On top of that, individual regions have layered their own rules: Moscow's mayor introduced fines of up to $700 for publishing photos of attacks, and Murmansk region decreed fines up to 1 million roubles for filming or sharing drone-strike-related content.
dead_ends.condition: During or shortly after a drone or military incident nearby

dead_ends.action: Fly a personal or hobby drone in a Russian city without prior authorization
dead_ends.why_fails: Operating an unmanned aircraft in Russia requires advance permission from the aviation authority, with flight route details submitted at least 24 hours ahead. Several regions have separately banned civilian drone flights outright since 2022 because of the war, so even a properly filed permit can still be refused in a banned zone.

workarounds.action: Default to not photographing anything that looks official, uniformed, or military - treat airports, checkpoints, and government buildings as off-limits unless clearly a designated tourist viewpoint

Never photograph, film, or share on social media anything related to a drone strike, air defense activity, or its aftermath, and check current regional decrees (Moscow, Murmansk, and others) rather than assuming only the national rule applies

To fly a drone, apply for aviation-authority permission and submit the flight route at least 24 hours in advance, and separately confirm the specific region has not banned civilian drone flights outright
